title: Ada and the Extraction
premise: Emrys Fairweather, a disgraced intelligence analyst, receives calls on a burner phone from Ada Lindqvist — a woman he loved and lost to a joint task force six years ago, who is officially dead. Ada is alive because she stole a ledger proving that a covert extraction program she once ran has been harvesting assets across three governments, and now the program's cleaner, an assassin called Voss, is erasing everyone who can read it. As Emrys smuggles Ada toward Frankfurt, where the ledger's financial fingerprints will detonate at market open, they rebuild the trust that duty once shattered. At dawn in Frankfurt, Emrys releases the ledger publicly while Ada trades herself to Voss to buy the upload time; Voss, discovering his own name in the ledger, lets her live and vanishes. The truth lands, three governments scramble, and Emrys and Ada walk away alive but unemployable — together, finally choosing each other over the institutions that used them.
about_author: Noor Kavanagh is a former financial-crimes researcher who left the field after a decade of watching quiet settlements bury loud crimes. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because they've watched them do it.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Emrys, scraping by on unattributable contract work in Lisbon, receives a burner phone in the mail with no sender. When it rings, the voice is Ada's — the woman whose funeral he attended. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into hunger; a man given one impossible second chance.

chapters.title: Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ada, hiding in a Trieste safehouse, explains the rules: short calls, moving numbers, never say her old name. She reveals she faked her death to escape the Meridian extraction program and has its ledger. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: guarded hope — she needs him but refuses to need him.

chapters.title: Ghost Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys uses his analyst skills to verify a fragment of the ledger and finds payment trails touching all three governments' black budgets. He realizes why no agency will ever claim this case. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the cold thrill of competence returning, shadowed by dread of what it costs.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: A Meridian archivist who helped Ada is found dead in Marseille, staged as a burglary. We meet Voss through his meticulous method and his unsettling habit of leaving victims' watches running. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: professional calm concealing a man who suspects he's next on someone's list.

chapters.title: Terms of Reunion
chapters.summary: Ada summons Emrys to Trieste against her own judgment. Their reunion is all tradecraft and old wounds: he never stopped looking for her; she let him grieve. They agree to move the ledger together. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love resurfacing under layers of resentment and duty.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Shape
chapters.summary: Emrys decodes the ledger's structure: it's indexed to accounts that mature at Frankfurt market open in nine days, when Meridian's funding vehicle rebalances. That's their window. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing into a plan with a hard deadline.

chapters.title: Old Colleagues, New Enemies
chapters.summary: Emrys approaches a former handler, Renata, for logistics; she warns him Meridian has friends inside every service and offers deniable help at a price. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being unclaimed by any institution.

chapters.title: Trieste Burns
chapters.summary: Meridian's cleaners hit the safehouse minutes after they leave. Ada's remaining contact, Matteo, dies covering their escape. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt compounding — everyone who helps her pays in full.

chapters.title: Night Train North
chapters.summary: On a sleeper train to Munich, Ada and Emrys finally speak honestly about the night she chose the mission over him. Walls crack; something like forgiveness begins. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt in transit, between borders where neither exists.

chapters.title: Munich Dead Drop
chapters.summary: They retrieve authentication keys for the ledger from a retired banker, only to find the drop already visited — Voss is hours behind them and knows their route. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the plan's margin of safety collapsing to zero.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Ada confesses the full truth: her 'death' was sanctioned, and she volunteered, believing it would protect Emrys. His anger breaks open into grief. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in other people's mourning.

chapters.title: Renata's Price
chapters.summary: Renata demands the ledger's section naming her own past dealings in exchange for exfiltration support. Emrys must decide whether trust is a currency he can still spend. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: moral erosion — using the enemy's logic to fight the enemy.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Doubt
chapters.summary: Voss reviews his kill list and finds anomalies: entries redacted above his clearance, including a name he recognizes as his own former identity. He begins pulling threads instead of cutting them. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: a weapon developing a conscience, or an agenda.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Arrivals
chapters.summary: They reach Frankfurt two days before market open and hole up with a journalist, Ilse, who agrees to hold the ledger's public release if they don't survive. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: found family assembling from strays — Ilse, Renata's courier, even a sympathetic clerk.

chapters.title: Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: Meridian makes contact through an intermediary: Ada's full pardon and restored identity in exchange for the ledger and Emrys's silence. It's everything she officially died wanting. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: temptation as a mirror — the life offered is built on the lie she'd be accepting.

chapters.title: Ilse's Question
chapters.summary: Ilse stress-tests the story, finding a gap that suggests a fourth government quietly bankrolled Meridian's founding. The stakes escalate beyond scandal into potential war-footing cover-ups. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: vertigo — the truth is bigger than the truth they planned to tell.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bourse
chapters.summary: Renata sells their location to Meridian to erase her own ledger entry. A firefight in the financial district scatters the group; Ilse is wounded shielding the drive. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: betrayal confirming Emrys's oldest wound — institutions eat their own.

chapters.title: Voss Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Voss corners Ada alone but reveals the redactions: Meridian scheduled him for disposal after Frankfurt. He offers a temporary alliance — not mercy, arithmetic. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: the assassin choosing survival over obedience, the book's thesis embodied.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes to Open
chapters.summary: Dawn. The team splits: Emrys and Ilse race to upload the ledger via the bourse's press room; Ada walks into Meridian's forward base offering herself to stall the response teams. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — she surrenders so the truth doesn't have to.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: At 9:00 CET the ledger goes live globally; Meridian's funding vehicle craters mid-auction. In the base, Voss turns on his own handlers rather than execute Ada, buying her exit at gunpoint. POV: Emrys and Voss. Emotional beat: climax — chaos as liberation, the markets doing what governments wouldn't.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unattributed
chapters.summary: Three governments issue bland denials; inquiries bloom and are quietly pruned. Renata disappears. Voss vanishes with a copy of the ledger as insurance. Emrys and Ada, officially nonexistent, watch the fallout from a Lisbon rooftop. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: hollow victory turning warm — they kept nothing but each other, and it's enough.

chapters.title: Ada and the Extraction
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a new burner arrives: someone inside another program wants out, and only the pair who broke Meridian can extract them. Ada looks at Emrys; he answers the phone. POV: both. Emotional beat: resolution as beginning — found family becoming a vocation, survival becoming a choice they keep making.
